facts.statement: The named species S. polyspondyla was found in the Sinemurian-aged Blue Lias formation of Lyme Regis, England.
facts.quote: It contains a single named species known from the Sinemurian-aged Blue Lias of Lyme Regis, England

facts.statement: Complete fossil specimens representing both male and female individuals of S. polyspondyla are known.
facts.quote: complete specimens representing both males and females

facts.statement: A second species, S. tenuispina, known only from an isolated male horn, is now considered the same species as S. polyspondyla.
facts.quote: A second species from the same locality, S. tenuispina Woodward, 1886 (known from an isolated horn of a male), is now considered conspecific with S. polyspondyla.

facts.statement: A complete female specimen of an indeterminate Squaloraja species was found in the Sinemurian-aged Moltrasio Formation of Osteno, Italy.
facts.quote: the complete specimen of the female of an indeterminate species is known from the Sinemurian-aged Moltrasio Formation of Osteno, Italy

facts.statement: Indeterminate teeth of Squaloraja have been found in the earlier Hettangian period of Belgium.
facts.quote: indeterminate teeth are known from the earlier Hettangian of Belgium

facts.statement: Research suggests Squaloraja was a relict taxon and the last survivor of a chimaera lineage that diverged from Chimaeroidei by the late Mississippian stage of the Carboniferous period.
facts.quote: Divergence estimates suggest that Squaloraja was a relict taxon and the last surviving member of a chimaera lineage that had diverged from the Chimaeroidei by the late Mississippian stage of the Carboniferous period

facts.statement: The type specimen of Squaloraja was discovered by Mary Anning in 1829.
facts.quote: The type specimen was found by Mary Anning in 1829.

facts.statement: The type specimen was held at the Bristol Museum but was destroyed during The Blitz, except for the tail.
facts.quote: This specimen was held at the Bristol Museum, and aside from the tail, was destroyed during The Blitz.

facts.statement: Louis Agassiz described the species as Spinacorhinus polyspondylus in 1836 based on the same specimen.
facts.quote: In 1836, Louis Agassiz described the species as Spinacorhinus polyspondylus based on the same specimen.

facts.statement: Agassiz changed the genus name to Squaloraja in 1843 but kept his original species name.
facts.quote: Following the publishing of Riley's description, Agassiz amended the genus name in 1843 to Squaloraja, but retained his own species name.

facts.statement: Squaloraja belongs to the parent group Squalorajidae.
Squaloraja is classified in the family Squalorajidae.
Squaloraja is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Squaloraja lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)
